equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests at estimated fair value
equity_bridge.note: Book NCI $6,268M at 2026-07-31; Walmex ~30% minority at market ~US$16-17B, partly offset by loss-making Flipkart/PhonePe minorities carried near book. Deducted here because flows are consolidated.

Last tagged EquitySecuritiesFvNi $3,041M at FY2025 year-end, rolled for FY2026 +$1.5B unrealized gain / -$0.9B sales and H1 FY2027 -$0.8B loss -> ~$2.8B. Their gains/losses sit below operating income, so they are outside the flows and belong in the bridge.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (3.9%) diverges >30% from EPS 5yr (11.6%) and revenue 5yr (5.0%). Equity is suppressed by $43B of buybacks over FY2022-26 and EPS is flattered off an FY2023 base hit by equity-investment losses and opioid settlement charges, so neither is a clean growth proxy; revenue 5yr CAGR is used.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC). Owner FCF 3yr CAGR 2.8% vs reported 7.6%: SBC grew from $1.6B to $3.6B (FY2023-26), faster than FCF. 5yr FCF CAGRs are negative because FY2021 was a pandemic working-capital windfall and capex doubled from $10.3B to $26.6B (automation program) - capex intensity, not operating deterioration, is what compressed FCF. EPS split-adjusted for the Feb-2024 3:1 split (FY2021 4.75/3).

scenario_narratives.base: Walmart delivers its FY2027 guide (sales +4-5%, operating income +7-8.5%) and then grows sales mid-single-digit, fading to 3%, as U.S. share gains from higher-income trade-down and 20%+ e-commerce growth continue. Operating margin creeps from 4.2% to 5.3% over ten years because advertising (Walmart Connect, Vizio) and membership income grow 15-25% at high incremental margins, partly reinvested in price. The automation capex wave peaks in FY2027 at ~3.9% of sales and fades to 2.8%, which is where most of the FCF growth comes from. Even on this path owner FCF is ~$12-13B in FY2027 against an ~$830B market cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: The flywheel thesis plays out: advertising and marketplace scale toward Amazon-like economics, automated fulfillment brings e-commerce to store-level profitability, Flipkart/Walmex compound internationally, and sales grow 5%+ for five years. Operating margin reaches ~6.5% by Y10 - the level Costco/Amazon-retail-ex-AWS comparisons suggest is the ceiling for a grocery-heavy mix - while capex falls back under 2.7% of sales as the network is built.
scenario_narratives.bear: Tariffs on the ~third of U.S. merchandise that is imported, wage inflation and price competition from Amazon, Aldi and Temu force Walmart to reinvest every dollar of ad and membership profit into price; operating margin stays ~4.2% and sales growth slows to 2-3% as trade-down reverses. The automation program pays back slowly, so capex stays above 3% of sales. The business remains sound - this is a margin-stagnation case, not a solvency one.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Strict owner-FCF basis: SBC expensed, share count flat, operating leases inside EBITDA, finance leases and borrowings as debt, NCI at fair value in the bridge. Walmart trades at ~37x FY2027 guided EPS; the market is capitalising the advertising/membership mix shift and a post-capex-peak FCF recovery at far richer multiples than a 20x terminal cap at an 8% WACC allows. The model says plainly how much of today's price rests on the bull case.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value dominates: the 20x FCF cap binds in all scenarios; a higher exit multiple is the single biggest lever on value
Capex taper timing: every 0.5pp of sales of capex is ~$3.7B/yr of owner FCF
Operating-margin path depends on advertising/membership mix; tariff reinvestment can absorb it
NCI fair value is an estimate (Walmex market value, Flipkart/PhonePe at book)
Cash tax ramp: if 100% bonus depreciation keeps cash taxes near 18-20%, value is understated modestly

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 98.88-135.16
data_sources.financials: WMT_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL-derived) plus SEC companyfacts CIK 0000104169 for D&A, finance/operating lease liabilities and payments, NCI, short-term borrowings and Q2 FY2027 balance sheet (2026-07-31)
data_sources.qualitative: WMT_Analysis.json (2026-10-03): FY2027 guidance, advertising/membership growth, capex-peak commentary, tariff risk

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted-average shares, Q2 FY2027 10-Q (quarter ended 2026-07-31), 7,978M. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; buybacks ($8.1B FY2026, $5.1B H1 FY2027) more than fund the flat count.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K share-based compensation expense $3,603M (XBRL AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense; ties to CSV StockBasedComp). Walmart does not tag or separately present cash taxes withheld on net-share settlement (inside 'other financing activities'), and publishes no combined adjusted-EBITDA SBC line, so the expense figure is used alone; the understatement is small at ~0.5% of revenue SBC.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.7 for a grocery-anchored defensive retailer -> cost of equity ~7.7-8.0%; debt is ~6% of EV at an after-tax ~3.5%, so WACC ~7.8%, rounded to 8.0%. Same WACC in every scenario: margin, tariff and capex-payback risk are carried in the scenario flows, not in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: One treatment per lease class, never both. Operating leases (US GAAP straight-line rent, $2.4B FY2026 cost) are already charged inside operating income/EBITDA, so the $16.5B operating lease liability is EXCLUDED from net debt. Finance leases (depreciation in D&A, principal $0.9B in financing) are treated as debt: the $6.83B finance lease liability (0.88 current + 5.95 non-current) is IN total_debt, and the asset renewal is carried by the capex/D&A paths.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI charged once, in the bridge: flows are consolidated (Walmex ~30% minority, Flipkart/PhonePe minorities), and a -$15.0B fair-value NCI estimate is deducted in equity_bridge. Book NCI is $6.27B, but the Walmex minority alone is worth ~$16-17B at market; Flipkart/PhonePe minorities carry losses (FY2026 NCI income $377M, FY2025 $721M). The flows are not made attributable-only, so no NCI leakage is in the tax path.
inputs.net_debt_detail: 2026-07-31 (Q2 FY2027 10-Q): short-term borrowings 10,479 + long-term debt due within one year 3,470 + long-term debt 36,462 + finance lease obligations 880 + 5,952 = 57,243 total debt; cash 11,529; net debt 45,714. Short-term borrowings rose from 6,596 at FY2026 year-end (commercial paper funding capex + buybacks).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (routing table row 1/2: operating company; US filer, but leases and NCI adaptations applied). Walmart is a standard operating retailer whose value is a free-cash-flow stream; none of the bank/REIT/LIC/holdco rows apply. First valuation of WMT (no memory entry, no prior DCF). FY0 = FY2026 (ended 2026-01-31); Y1 = FY2027, which is guided at +4-5% cc sales and +7-8.5% cc operating income. Owner FCF FY2026 = reported FCF 14,923 (OCF 41,565 - capex 26,642) - SBC 3,603 - interest income 0 (Walmart is net DEBT, so no interest-income strip) = 11,320. FY0 component anchors: operating income 29,825 (4.18% of revenue, post-SBC), D&A 14,203 (1.99%), SBC 3,603 (0.51%) -> pre-SBC adjusted EBITDA 47,631 (6.68%); capex 26,642 (3.74%, cyclical peak of the automation/remodel program); cash taxes paid 5,364 = 18% of EBIT, depressed by bonus depreciation on the capex wave vs a 24.4% GAAP rate. Buybacks: Walmart is a funded repurchaser ($8.1B FY2026, $5.1B H1 FY2027), so the flat count is paid for in cash. 3:1 split Feb-2024: CSV share counts and EPS are split-adjusted from FY2022. Data note: CSV has no EBITDA after FY2019; D&A FY2026 taken from XBRL DepreciationAmortizationAndAccretionNet. Analysis.json labels the Q2 FY2027 Aug-2026 quarter as 'reported Aug 2025' - the figures (revenue $187.9B) are FY2027 Q2.

bear.ebitda_margin_path_note: Operating margin stuck ~4.1-4.2%: ad and membership gains are reinvested in price against tariffs, Amazon and Aldi/Temu; e-commerce mix keeps diluting.

base.ebitda_margin_path_note: Pre-SBC adjusted EBITDA = post-SBC operating margin + D&A% + SBC%. Operating margin 4.30% FY2027 (guided +7-8.5% op income on +4-5% sales from 4.18%), rising ~15bp/yr to 5.3% by Y10 as advertising (~$6.4B, +46%) and membership fees take mix share - roughly management's 'op income grows faster than sales' framing, not more.
base.capex_pct_path_note: FY2027 capex tracking ~$29B (H1 $14.2B) = 3.9% of sales, management says near peak; fades to 2.8% vs a 2.0-2.5% FY2015-21 history, leaving capex above D&A in perpetuity to fund 3% growth.
base.cash_tax_rate_path_note: FY2026 cash taxes 18% of EBIT (bonus depreciation on peak capex); ramps toward ~23.5% as capex normalises, still below the 24.4% GAAP rate because 100% expensing persists.
base.wc_capture_pct_note: Retailer with payables > inventory: growth releases a small amount of cash (positive capture), modest at 2% of incremental sales.

bull.ebitda_margin_path_note: Operating margin 4.35% -> 6.55% by Y10: advertising scales toward ~$20B at very high incremental margin, e-commerce reaches fulfillment-cost parity with stores on automation.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (up from the 15% default): tariff and price-investment risk is live and management is already reinvesting tariff refunds in H2 FY2027 price rather than margin. Base 50%: tracks guidance. Bull 30% (down from 35%): it needs both the ad/membership mix shift AND a fast capex taper to land together.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
